behavioral_notes.observation: The substance of html_editor is a static OWL/JS rich-text editor engine, NOT Python models. The Editor class attaches to a contenteditable element, topologically sorts a dependency-ordered list of Plugin subclasses, then wires them through a frozen 'resources' registry exposing dispatchTo (event fan-out), delegateTo (first-truthy command override) and checkPredicates (predicate voting). ~50 plugins are grouped into CORE_PLUGINS (Sanitize, Selection, History, Delete, Split, Clipboard, Format, Dom, Overlay, ProtectedNode, ...), MAIN_PLUGINS (Toolbar, Powerbox '/' command menu, Table, List, Link, Media/Image/Video, Font/Color, Banner, Emoji, Column, ...), COLLABORATION_PLUGINS and EMBEDDED_COMPONENT_PLUGINS (table-of-content, toggle-block, syntax-highlighting, caption, embedded video). The HtmlField OWL widget (registry fields:html) and Wysiwyg mount this engine inside forms; getContent runs clean_for_save_handlers before persistence. None of this architecture is visible in Python metadata (gap #3).

Provides field-level version history for sanitized Html fields. On write of a versioned field (declared via _get_versioned_fields, which MUST be sanitize=True or it raises ValidationError), it diffs old vs new content with generate_patch (diff_utils) and prepends a reverse patch {patch, revision_id, create_date, create_uid, create_user_name} into the html_field_history Json column, capped at 300 revisions (_html_field_history_size_limit), then calls super().write a second time to persist the new revision. html_field_history_get_content_at_revision replays patches with apply_patch to reconstruct any past revision, and *_get_comparison / *_get_unified_diff produce visual diffs. This document-versioning side-effect is invisible to metadata.

Collaborative editing rides the bus: the client subscribes to channels matching editor_collaboration:<model>:<field>:<res_id>; ir.websocket parses that pattern and authorizes the subscription only after check_access('read') AND check_access('write') on the document plus _check_field_access on the field (public users denied via AccessDenied). The /html_editor/bus_broadcast jsonrpc route re-runs the same access checks then bus.bus._sendone broadcasts peer edit ops/cursors on the (db,'editor_collaboration',model,field,res_id) channel. /get_ice_servers returns mail.ice.server records for the WebRTC peer transport. Cross-module side-effects (bus.bus + mail.ice.server) not derivable from html_editor's own models.

html_editor extends ir.attachment with computed image_src/image_width/image_height/local_url and an original_id link to the unoptimized source, so the media dialog and image-shape routes can serve optimized/resized/cropped variants (image_process, webp). /modify_image writes a derived attachment keeping original_id; /shape and /image_shape recolor SVG shapes by substituting palette colors pulled from the web.assets_frontend CSS bundle (with hex/rgba injection guards to prevent arbitrary CSS). /generate_text proxies the editor 'AI' feature to Odoo's OLG IAP endpoint (olg.api.odoo.com) via iap_tools.iap_jsonrpc with the database uuid; link_preview routes call mail.tools.link_preview; /video_url/data hits YouTube/Vimeo/Dailymotion oEmbed. These outbound calls and the attachment side-effects are metadata-invisible (gap #7).

value_streams: Compose-to-Persist: open Html field -> Editor plugins -> sanitized content -> ORM write (+ optional version snapshot)
Insert-Media: pick/upload media -> ir.attachment optimize -> embed referencing /web/image

policies: Versioned Html fields MUST be sanitize=True (ValidationError otherwise); collaboration bus channels require check_access read+write on the document and field (_check_field_access), public users denied; SVG shape recoloring guards against arbitrary color injection (hex/rgba whitelist); editor content passes the Sanitize plugin / server-side sanitize before persistence
stakeholders: End user / content author (writes rich text in any Html field)
Module developer (embeds HtmlField/Wysiwyg, writes editor plugins, declares versioned fields)
Website / Knowledge / Mail composer (consumes the editor as its text surface)
metrics: Revision count per versioned field (html_field_history, capped 300); upload progress toast; AI request quota (limit_call_reached from OLG endpoint)

classification.rationale: html_editor is technical UI-framework infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'), not a value-creating primary activity of any chain/shop/network. It is the shared rich-text/WYSIWYG editing component and plugin framework that mail, website, knowledge, mass_mailing and other modules embed wherever an Html field is edited; auto_install=true (depends base/bus/web) makes it ubiquitous editor plumbing. Like web, its substance is the FRONTEND layer: ~187 JS files / ~58 XML templates, ~40 catalogued OWL components and an Editor-plus-~50-plugin engine (gap #3), versus only ~2 real own Python models (html.field.history.mixin + test models) and ~5 inherit-only ORM extensions (ir.attachment, ir.qweb.field.*, ir.ui.view, ir.http, ir.websocket) — the inverse of a data-bearing business module. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' fits because html_editor is an IT-delivery / application-platform capability (it delivers a reusable client UI component plus its media/collaboration plumbing). 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' was the auto-architect baseline guess and was considered (the editor is a platform other capabilities build on) but rejected: html_editor is a concrete running UI runtime/component, not a governance/portfolio capability — its work is IT delivery, squarely 8.0.

standard_capabilities: Reusable OWL rich-text editor (HtmlField widget + Wysiwyg) with a dependency-ordered plugin framework
Powerbox '/' command menu, toolbar, tables, lists, links, fonts/colors, emoji, banners, columns
Media management: image upload/optimize/resize/crop, video oEmbed (YouTube/Vimeo/Dailymotion), SVG shape recoloring, Odoo media library search
HTML field versioning (diff/patch history, restore & visual comparison)
Real-time collaborative editing over the bus (+ WebRTC ICE servers)
In-place QWeb field editing with conversion of edits back to Odoo records
Embedded components (table of contents, toggle blocks, syntax highlighting, captions)
AI text generation in the editor via Odoo OLG IAP
typical_fits: Drop an Html field with the editor into any form/model with zero editor plumbing
Use the media dialog and image pipeline out of the box (website, mail, knowledge)
Enable field history by overriding _get_versioned_fields on a sanitize=True Html field
common_gaps: Custom editor plugins / commands / embedded components (requires JS dev, gap #3)
Bespoke sanitization / allowed-tag policies beyond the default Sanitize plugin
Self-hosted or alternative AI provider instead of the Odoo OLG IAP endpoint
External integrations are limited to Odoo IAP/media + public oEmbed/CDN hosts (gap #7), not arbitrary third-party CMS/editor services
